transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-19 10:00 PDT
- Duration: 52 mins
- Attendees: Jamie Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Omar Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lila Chen (Nimbus CTO), Rajiv Menon (Nimbus Eng Manager), Sophie Park (Nimbus Security), Tom Alvarez (Nimbus Platform)

[00:00] Jamie (AE): okay uh hey everyone thanks for joining on a Monday morning, appreciate it. We're gonna run quick, this is a readi- readiness / risk quick sync, think of it like a lightning all-hands for the pilot.
[00:12] Dr. Lila Chen: thanks Jamie, we have about 50 minutes, tough schedule but good to cover the safety bits first.
[00:18] Sophie (Security): yes, PHI is the big one for us, Qs around encryption at rest and in transit, key management, and audit trails. also curious about your SOC2 status and if you can do an on-prem option.
[00:29] Jamie (AE): absolutely. to set expectations we are SOC2 Type II certified — I'll share the report — and we offer Private (VPC) deployments or on-prem packages for air-gapped setups. Maya will walk through network + KMS options.
[00:42] Maya (SE): hi all. so briefly, there are three typical modes: hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc. hosted is fastest to start but we know for PHI folks the private or dedicated path is common. for KMS we integrate with AWS KMS & GCP KMS, and HSM for some enterprise deals.
[01:05] Tom (Platform): quick q — for VPC, is it customer-managed peering or do you provide a managed VPN?
[01:11] Maya (SE): we support both: VPC peering and customer-managed transit gateway, also dedicated private link. sometimes the terminology gets scrambled in our docs, sorry if you saw mixed language.
[01:23] Rajiv (Eng): on perf: we intend to run long-context gen workloads, 6-8k tokens, sometimes with streaming. need sub-300ms token latency at steady state for completion token generation. is that realistic?
[01:34] Maya (SE): it's, uh, depends on model choice and quantization. with optimized kernels and a Dedicated pool on A100/H100 variants you can get steady low latency for many production setups. for streaming there are tradeoffs — batching helps cost but can increase tail latency.
[01:50] Omar (CSM): and we can simulate your QPS pattern in a benchmark run, we'll propose a bench plan.
[01:56] Dr. Lila Chen: we'll need repeatable runs — same prompt set, same seed if possible, and we'll expect logging and some raw token timing.
[02:08] Jamie (AE): noted. we'll ask Rajiv to send the prompt set and target QPS.
[02:12] Rajiv (Eng): yes sending after.

[02:20] Sophie (Security): on audit logs, do you preserve token-level logs or only metadata? retention windows? we cannot retain PHI in logs — need redaction.
[02:31] Maya (SE): good call. by default the hosted API logs full payloads for diagnostics, but for enterprise we can disable token-level retention, support on-the-fly redaction, and stream minimal audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or Kinesis. that's configurable per route.
[02:50] Sophie: perfect. also SSO — SAML + SCIM?
[02:54] Jamie: yes SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC for roles. we'll include the admin onboarding docs.

[03:05] Tom (Platform): what's the fallback strategy if a model variant is overloaded? our app needs graceful degradation.
[03:12] Maya: routing policies — we have automatic fallback to compatible smaller quantized model variants or a lower-cost region. also configurable canary rollouts and timeouts. caveat: smaller variants might have occasional quality regressions, we can tie regressions to evals.
[03:30] Dr. Lila: quality is important. we cannot accept hallucinations around dosages. does Redwood provide eval tooling to baseline quality?
[03:39] Jamie: yes we have Redwood Optimize and eval harness to run prompt sets and surface regressions; we'll share a sample eval report.

[03:50] Rajiv: can you outline the procurement path? we likely need a POC agreement, security review, then dedicated capacity order.
[03:58] Omar: typical path is POC -> security attestation + SOC2 + network review -> pilot order (month) -> ramp to reserved/dedicated if SLA needed. procurement timelines vary, but pushing a pilot within 2-4 weeks is common.
[04:14] Sophie: need a legal point on data residency; we are in US and EU — how are regions mapped?
[04:20] Maya: we can pin regions at route level. hosted model catalog shows region availability; Dedicated gives you region guarantees depending on capacity.

[04:32] Jamie: quick numbers: pilot baseline for Dedicated benchmarking includes 2-4 GPUs for a small pool; pricing depends on model family, quantization, and peak qps. I'll send a rough estimate but Maya will follow with a more detailed latency/cost calc per region.
[04:50] Rajiv: fine. also latency targets — sub-300ms per token — is that per token or per request?
[04:56] Maya: per token generation latency. again depends on sequence length and batching. long prefix caching (KV cache) helps repeated conversation context.

[05:10] Tom: are logs shipable to our SIEM? we need structured traces for audit.
[05:15] Maya: yes structured tracing and per-request metadata; we've got tracing hooks and an observability endpoint that streams to your logging stack. sometimes the agent name in the trace is mis- spelled in older runs — we've fixed most of that.

[05:30] Dr. Lila: any special controls around model updates? We need version pinning.
[05:35] Jamie: yes pin models per route, can roll forward with canary, A/B tests, automatic fallback on regression.

[05:45] Rajiv: one more technical — does Redwood support GPU quantization modes we can test? e.g. 4-bit, 8-bit for cost tradeoffs?
[05:53] Maya: yes we have several quantization profiles. note 4-bit can save cost but sometimes impacts quality; we'll recommend model+quant combo for your prompts.

[06:05] Sophie: what about encryption keys? customer-managed KMS means we never hand you keys?
[06:10] Maya: customer-managed KMS lets you rotate keys in your cloud, Redwood holds only ciphertext; for on-prem we can use HSM connectors.

[06:20] Jamie: okay let's capture next steps — short recap.
[06:25] Omar: Action: Jamie to share SOC2 and network diagram.
[06:28] Jamie: yep.
[06:30] Rajiv: Action: I'll share the prompt set and qps profile.
[06:34] Sophie: Action: security team will send any questionnaire — but we need to see retention configs first.
[06:38] Tom: can we schedule the perf bench run?
[06:40] Maya: suggest 7/28 or earlier; I think 7/24 works for an initial pricing + bench plan sync.

[06:48] Dr. Lila: thanks all, this was helpful. any open items for leadership?
[06:52] Jamie: none from us, we'll follow up with the docs and the bench plan. thanks everyone.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-phrases of product names and acronyms, some timestamps approximated; speaker labels mostly accurate but may include one ambiguous label (Speaker 6) from the calendar export.
